correctness.rationale: For all n>=1 a no-valley pair implication forbids every nonnested two-query support; for strictly nested pairs an explicit sequence of endpoint deletions with independent consecutive pair blocks gives a complete fixed-complement subcube. Counting rainbow nested perfect matchings on any chosen 2k axis points gives the polynomial and exact VC dimension; extreme-pair deletion gives all 2^(n-1) online tree paths, matched by the finite-cardinality bound. For every k, explicit integer-valued utility samples with peak at k+1/2 and independent ±1 offsets are strictly monotone on each side, and continuous piecewise-linear interpolation yields a counterexample to finite continuous VC. The actual checker independently verified 132154 support instances, full branch paths through 12 alternatives, and 4094 fixed-peak utility assignments; infinite claims are proved, not extrapolated.

originality.rationale: Direct primary-text comparison found the standard fixed-axis preference sign coding and elicitation algorithms but not the exact rainbow-nesting support complex, strong subcubes, polynomial, or exact VC/Littlestone pair. The continuous construction contradicts a concrete published illustrative finite-VC assertion under that paper’s stated real-utility definition. published-finding corpus semantic searches across aliases/parameters returned no stronger covering record. All work may have prior equivalents under other terminology; the cited historical risk remains.
residual_risks: Undiscovered alternative equivalent language for strongly shattered nested pairs or maximum/lopsided preference domains might change novelty priority.
The published 2020 illustrative finite-VC statement is distinguished carefully from unrelated main utility-under-uncertainty results; no claim is made that their general results are invalid.
Conitzer 2009 and older preference-domain structure are recognized as background, not claimed as new.
Theorem applies only to a fixed axis and all strict compatible orders; continuous argument needs unrestricted shape, not common slope/distance models.

value.rationale: The theorem supplies an exact all-coefficient and strongly shattered support classification for a natural learning class, proves shattering-extremality and linearly diverging adaptive versus static complexity, and provides a counterexample to an explicit real-single-peaked finite-VC assertion in the learning literature. The main facts are structurally motivated by preference elicitation and falsifiability; ordinary 2^(n-1) vote counting is excluded from the novelty claim.
